scenes.headline: How Qwen Audio 3.0 turns text into a voice
scenes.sub: An autoregressive LM, a flow-matching decoder, and a 12.5 Hz tokenizer.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Butterscotch! Qwen Audio 3.0 tops the Artificial Analysis speech leaderboard. Here's how it turns text into a voice.

scenes.text: Split the job: a language model decides what is said, as a short stream of speech tokens. A flow-matching decoder decides how it sounds.

scenes.title: From text to a 48 kHz waveform

steps.say: Text goes in with a free-style instruction and inline tags. An autoregressive model predicts speech tokens, one per step.
Those tokens come from a supervised speech tokenizer, which fronts the whole stack. To clone a voice, a reference clip conditions the model too.
A flow-matching decoder turns the tokens into a mel spectrogram. Content was the model's job; voice and prosody are this one's.
A vocoder rebuilds the waveform, and super-resolves it to forty-eight kilohertz.

scenes.title: Why 12.5 Hz
scenes.text: decode steps = seconds of audio x 12.5 Hz
scenes.say: Why the frame rate matters so much:

parts.note: one token per step, strictly in order
parts.say: Each step emits one token, in order, so fewer tokens per second means less waiting.

parts.note: most speech codecs sit at 25 to 75 Hz
parts.say: Most codecs run at twenty-five to seventy-five hertz. At twelve point five, a supervised tokenizer keeps just the content and speaker detail the model needs.

items.say: Pretrain the language model and decoder separately.
Train them jointly, annealing on high-quality data.
Give the language model a reinforcement learning pass.
Teach the decoder to cope with noisy prompts.
Then give the decoder its own reinforcement pass.

scenes.text: Good speech now hinges on the surfaces you expose: frame rate, instructions and tags, more than the core generative trick.

recap: An LM for what, a flow decoder for how
A 12.5 Hz supervised tokenizer keeps it fast
Instructions and 86 inline tags steer delivery
scenes.say: To recap: content from the language model, voice from the decoder, and a slow tokenizer that keeps it quick.
